question: In dravidian style of temples the main temple tower is known as ___________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**vimana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Dravidian style of temples, the main temple tower is known as **vimana**.
 
• The **vimana** is the sanctum sanctorum where the main deity is enshrined and is usually topped with a dome-like structure.
 
• The **gopuram** is the monumental entrance tower, typically ornate, found at the entrance of the temple complex.
 
• The **mandapa** refers to the pillared hall or pavilion for public rituals and ceremonies.
 
• The **shikhara** is a term used in the Nagara style of temple architecture, referring to the rising tower in the sanctum sanctorum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Dravidian style** of temple architecture is prominent in South India.
 
• This architectural style evolved under the patronage of various South Indian dynasties such as the Cholas, Pallavas, and Pandyas.
 
• Characteristic features of Dravidian temples include large gopurams, intricate carvings, and expansive temple complexes.
 
• Famous examples of Dravidian temples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai.
